
=================================================================
#63 Tribute  (498)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Fall of Euija · tone: island folklore chronicle
Logline: The tribute boat comes home from Sabi with the king’s news. None of it has Gyebek’s name in it.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ The tribute boat comes home light. The oranges stayed in Sabi. The news did not.
[1] ¶ Gyebek is on the sand before the sail has a shape. The captain holds a Yunbi contract and has been told not to talk to him. He talks anyway. It is a long way to sail with a thing like that in your mouth.
[2] The Captain: The rite is over, General. Done at the new year. / His Majesty calls the Assembly on the first of the month. All eight houses.
[3] Gyebek: Did he send for me.
[4] The Captain: …… / Nobody said your name, General.
[5] Gyebek: Did anyone say it.
[6] The Captain: No. / …Your wife came to the berth when we docked. She said to tell you— / the boy counts too.
[7] ¶ Gyebek thanks him exactly once. He walks up the beach to the beam by the door, where the notches have run out. Nothing. He has never had a number end on him before.
[8] ── SCENE: The Forgotten Oranges ──
[9] Gyebek: Why does your island keep Baekje’s men. / You owe Baekje nothing.
[10] Yuri Dora: Owe nothing? Ha. Once, long ago, we forgot the oranges.
[11] ¶ One year, long ago, Tamla stops sending tribute. Rebellion would at least have been legible. This is closer to forgetting, which a large kingdom finds harder to forgive.
[12] ¶ Baekje’s king marches an army to the southern harbour and stops. He lets the news cross the water on its own. It gets there faster than he would have.
[13] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 26, Baekje Annals — King Dongseong, yr. 20 (498), eighth month): Eighth month. Because Tamla had not sent its tribute, the king went out to punish it himself and got as far as Mujin Province. Tamla heard, sent envoys to beg pardon, and he stopped.❞
[14] Yuri Dora: See what he did? He marched to the harbour, and stopped. / He didn’t want to cross. He wanted us to know he could.
[15] ¶ Tamla apologises. Baekje accepts. Nobody is killed, everybody is satisfied, and the oranges resume. For a hundred and fifty years, that is the whole relationship.
[16] ¶ So when Baekje needs somewhere to put a man it cannot kill, there is an island, and the island owes it a favour.
[17] Gyebek: His Majesty will cross. / After the Assembly.
[18] Yuri Dora: Turtle. A king who marches to the harbour and stops is telling you something.
[19] Gyebek: His Majesty has not marched to the harbour. / So he has not stopped.
[20] ¶ Yuri Dora opens his mouth, and shuts it. There is no answer to that. There is only the next morning.
[21] ¶ He has run out of days to count. So at dawn he goes down to the black rock and starts counting something else.
[22] ── SCENE: Black Rock ──
[23] ¶ He trains at the same hour on the same slab of lava on the eastern shore, and when the tide takes that slab he waits for the tide rather than use another one.
[24] Yuri Dora: The next rock is the same.
[25] Gyebek: It is not the same.
[26] ¶ The rock is porous and cruel and nothing like a drill ground. You cannot plant a foot on it twice in the same place. Two seasons of it and he no longer needs to know where his feet are.
[27] The Divers: You don’t hold the breath. You push it out with singing.
[28] Gyebek: …I cannot sing.
[29] The Divers: Nobody cannot. There are only people who don’t.
[30] ¶ The village children learn the count of his drills before they learn his name, and stand on the rocks doing it badly behind him, and he does not once turn round to stop them, because stopping would be an interruption and he does not interrupt.
[31] [MORAL the warning: A man who cannot vary anything will be unbeatable on the ground he chose, and helpless on any other. Give him the choosing.]
[32] ── SCENE: Five Thousand ──
[33] ¶ He is asked, once, why he counts everything, and he answers honestly, which is the only way he has ever answered anything.
[34] Gyebek: Numbers do not lie to me.
[35] Yuri Dora: And people do?
[36] Gyebek: People are not trying to. / I simply do not follow them. / I have never learned to read a face.
[37] Yuri Dora: Then how did you survive twenty years at a court?
[38] Gyebek: I trusted one man.
[39] ¶ The island considers this the saddest sentence anybody has said on it, and nobody explains to him why they have all gone quiet, and he does not ask, because he has not noticed.
[40] ?: (Tamla fisher, laughing) / Hundred-Victories, they call him on the mainland — and here he counts oranges like they might desert.
[41] ¶ He drills in units of five hundred. One day he will take ten of those units to a field and leave the rest behind. The count is already in his mouth.
[42] ¶ That night he cuts a new notch at the other end of the beam. One. If the king sends, he will be ready. If the king does not send, he will be ready.
[43] ¶ **Meanwhile, in Sabi, Euija calls the Assembly. He has a smile, a speech, and a proclamation printed before anyone sat down…!**
